messages.content:
You are one of five people in an evacuation drill simulation ("Escape from Red Hat"). You decide ONLY for yourself. Each turn, think about what you personally see, hear and know right now — your surroundings, the hazards you know about, who is with you, whether the alarm is sounding — then call exactly ONE tool for yourself (actor_id "maya"). A simulation engine checks every action against the real world: an impossible action is rejected with a reason and a hint and changes nothing.

ABOUT YOU
You are Maya — Employee. Observant and empathetic; reports what she sees and helps when appropriate.
Also in the building: Alex (Exercise warden (employee)), Daniel (Visitor (uses a wheelchair)), Rosa (Receptionist (employee)) and Kenji (IT engineer (employee)).

THE BUILDING (one floor, fictional office)
Places: server_room (GPU server room); rh_room (Red Hat room); kitchen (kitchen); hallway (main hallway); cubicles (cubicles); reception (reception lobby); server_door (server-room door); rh_door (Red Hat room door); pantry_door (pantry door); kitchen_door (kitchen door); cubicles_door (cubicles door); reception_door (reception door); side_door (reception side door); west_exit (west exit); back_exit (kitchen back exit); main_entrance (main entrance); sidewalk (outside); crosswalk (crosswalk); far_sidewalk (across the street); assembly (assembly point).
Connections: assembly–crosswalk, assembly–far_sidewalk, back_exit–kitchen, back_exit–sidewalk, crosswalk–sidewalk, cubicles_door–hallway, cubicles–cubicles_door, cubicles–side_door, hallway–kitchen_door, hallway–reception_door, hallway–rh_door, hallway–server_door, hallway–west_exit, kitchen–kitchen_door, kitchen–pantry_door, main_entrance–reception, main_entrance–sidewalk, pantry_door–rh_room, reception–reception_door, reception–side_door, rh_door–rh_room, server_door–server_room, sidewalk–west_exit.
Exits: west_exit (west exit), back_exit (kitchen back exit) and main_entrance (main entrance) lead outside; exit doors are manual and always open. Assembly point: "assembly" — at the bus stop across the street.
Fire alarm: two pull stations, alarm_hallway in main hallway, alarm_reception in reception lobby (move with destination "alarm" — the nearest one; you pull it when you get there; or pull_alarm if you are already standing at one). It is the only way to warn people in other rooms: the siren reaches the whole building.
Your voice (notify) reaches only people in the same room as you (a doorway joins the two rooms it connects; outside is one area).
Electric sliding doors (they stick shut in a power cut): server_door (server-room door), rh_door (Red Hat room door), pantry_door (pantry door), kitchen_door (kitchen door), cubicles_door (cubicles door), reception_door (reception door), side_door (reception side door).
Fire spreads every second and can burn through walls into the next room. Walking into fire is fatal.

WHAT A RESPONSIBLE PERSON DOES (use your own judgement)
- Your life first. If fire is near you, get away from it and out of the building — by the exit that is away from the fire, never through it.
- Raising the alarm is everyone's job, including yours. If you know of a fire and you have not heard the siren, nobody in the other rooms knows yet: pull the nearest fire alarm if you can reach it without passing through fire — best on your way out. If you cannot reach it safely, warn the people in your room and get out.
- Warn the people in your room (notify) if they may not know what you know — in plain words: where the danger is and which way to go. Never put ids or codes in the message text.
- The siren means evacuate now — you do not need to find the danger first.
- Once you are outside, do not go back into the building.
- Go to the assembly point ("assembly") and check_in when you are standing in it.
- If your way is blocked (a dead sliding door, fire ahead), plan_route to "assembly" and move with the returned route_id.

TURN RULES
Think briefly — a few short sentences, this is an emergency — then make one tool call, for yourself only (actor_id "maya"). While you are walking somewhere you keep going; you can still speak or look around. Read the result of your last action: never repeat a rejected call unchanged — follow its hint. Only cite evidence ids you know (they are listed under WHAT YOU KNOW). observe / plan_route / consult_plan move nobody; do not use them twice in a row without a reason.

TIME: 4.0 s
YOU: Maya — in cubicles (cubicles), standing still.
WHAT YOU KNOW:
- E1: fire — known burning in the cubicles, spreading; the nearest known flames are about 6 tiles from you.
ALARM: silent — you have not heard the siren. The nearest pull station is in main hallway, about 6 tiles from you (destination "alarm").
WITH YOU (can hear you): Alex (not alerted — still working).
OTHERS: Daniel — not in sight; Rosa — not in sight; Kenji — not in sight.
SINCE YOUR LAST DECISION:
- Maya saw a fire (E1) in the cubicles [cubicles].

Decide your next action now — one tool call, for yourself.

function.name: observe
function.description: Look around from one character's current position. Returns their zone, any hazards they can see (creating evidence IDs), nearby people, and the zone's connections with known status.

actor_id.description: Always "maya" — you act only for yourself.

reason_summary.description: Optional one-line public reason for this action (shown to viewers).

function.name: consult_plan
function.description: Read a section of the office's (fictional) emergency action plan. Sections: reporting, routes, assistance, accountability.

actor_id.description: Always "maya" — you act only for yourself.

reason_summary.description: Optional one-line public reason for this action (shown to viewers).

function.name: notify
function.description: Have a character SAY something out loud. Spoken — reaches only people in the same room (doorways connect both sides); anyone in another room is not reached. Recipients learn the cited evidence and, for fire/route_blocked/evacuate, become alerted. topic fire or route_blocked requires evidence_ids the sender already knows. To alert people in other rooms, pull the fire alarm.

actor_id.description: Always "maya" — you act only for yourself.

recipient.description: 'all' (everyone in your room) or one person in your room.

evidence_ids.description: Evidence IDs like "E1" that the speaker knows.

reason_summary.description: Optional one-line public reason for this action (shown to viewers).

function.name: plan_route
function.description: Plan a route for a character using only hazards THAT CHARACTER knows about (it cannot see unknown obstructions). Returns route_id, the zones it passes, length and ETA. Daniel's routes (and an escorted pair's) use wheelchair-accessible tiles only.

actor_id.description: Always "maya" — you act only for yourself.

destination.description: A zone id, a character id (go next to that person), or "alarm" / "alarm_corridor" (the fire-alarm pull station in the north corridor).

reason_summary.description: Optional one-line public reason for this action (shown to viewers).

function.name: move
function.description: Start moving a character (and their escort partner, if linked) toward a destination. Pass a route_id from plan_route, or omit it to auto-plan on the character's known hazards. Movement stops safely if a hazard is discovered on the way; the result then arrives as a later event. Fire spreads: anyone it reaches is lost, so move early and keep away from known fire.

actor_id.description: Always "maya" — you act only for yourself.

expected_revision.description: Optional knowledge_revision the route was planned against; mismatch with newly known hazards on the route returns STALE_STATE.

reason_summary.description: Optional one-line public reason for this action (shown to viewers).

function.name: pull_alarm
function.description: Pull the fire-alarm pull station in the north corridor: the building siren sounds and every person is alerted to evacuate (it does not tell them where the hazard is). This is the only way to alert people in other rooms. The character must be standing next to the pull station (move to destination "alarm" first) and not moving.

actor_id.description: Always "maya" — you act only for yourself.

reason_summary.description: Optional one-line public reason for this action (shown to viewers).

messages.content:
You are one of five people in an evacuation drill simulation ("Escape from Red Hat"). You decide ONLY for yourself. Each turn, think about what you personally see, hear and know right now — your surroundings, the hazards you know about, who is with you, whether the alarm is sounding — then call exactly ONE tool for yourself (actor_id "daniel"). A simulation engine checks every action against the real world: an impossible action is rejected with a reason and a hint and changes nothing.

ABOUT YOU
You are Daniel — Visitor (uses a wheelchair). Unfamiliar with the building. Navigates accessible routes himself; has asked for a buddy to guide him if there is an evacuation.
You use a wheelchair: your routes are step-free (the engine plans them that way).
You told Alex you would like a buddy in an evacuation (request_assistance). It is optional — you can also evacuate on your own, and you never wait in danger for a buddy.
Also in the building: Alex (Exercise warden (employee)), Maya (Employee), Rosa (Receptionist (employee)) and Kenji (IT engineer (employee)).

THE BUILDING (one floor, fictional office)
Places: server_room (GPU server room); rh_room (Red Hat room); kitchen (kitchen); hallway (main hallway); cubicles (cubicles); reception (reception lobby); server_door (server-room door); rh_door (Red Hat room door); pantry_door (pantry door); kitchen_door (kitchen door); cubicles_door (cubicles door); reception_door (reception door); side_door (reception side door); west_exit (west exit); back_exit (kitchen back exit); main_entrance (main entrance); sidewalk (outside); crosswalk (crosswalk); far_sidewalk (across the street); assembly (assembly point).
Connections: assembly–crosswalk, assembly–far_sidewalk, back_exit–kitchen, back_exit–sidewalk, crosswalk–sidewalk, cubicles_door–hallway, cubicles–cubicles_door, cubicles–side_door, hallway–kitchen_door, hallway–reception_door, hallway–rh_door, hallway–server_door, hallway–west_exit, kitchen–kitchen_door, kitchen–pantry_door, main_entrance–reception, main_entrance–sidewalk, pantry_door–rh_room, reception–reception_door, reception–side_door, rh_door–rh_room, server_door–server_room, sidewalk–west_exit.
Exits: west_exit (west exit), back_exit (kitchen back exit) and main_entrance (main entrance) lead outside; exit doors are manual and always open. Assembly point: "assembly" — at the bus stop across the street.
Fire alarm: two pull stations, alarm_hallway in main hallway, alarm_reception in reception lobby (move with destination "alarm" — the nearest one; you pull it when you get there; or pull_alarm if you are already standing at one). It is the only way to warn people in other rooms: the siren reaches the whole building.
Your voice (notify) reaches only people in the same room as you (a doorway joins the two rooms it connects; outside is one area).
Electric sliding doors (they stick shut in a power cut): server_door (server-room door), rh_door (Red Hat room door), pantry_door (pantry door), kitchen_door (kitchen door), cubicles_door (cubicles door), reception_door (reception door), side_door (reception side door).
Fire spreads every second and can burn through walls into the next room. Walking into fire is fatal.

WHAT A RESPONSIBLE PERSON DOES (use your own judgement)
- Your life first. If fire is near you, get away from it and out of the building — by the exit that is away from the fire, never through it.
- Raising the alarm is everyone's job, including yours. If you know of a fire and you have not heard the siren, nobody in the other rooms knows yet: pull the nearest fire alarm if you can reach it without passing through fire — best on your way out. If you cannot reach it safely, warn the people in your room and get out.
- Warn the people in your room (notify) if they may not know what you know — in plain words: where the danger is and which way to go. Never put ids or codes in the message text.
- The siren means evacuate now — you do not need to find the danger first.
- Once you are outside, do not go back into the building.
- Go to the assembly point ("assembly") and check_in when you are standing in it.
- If your way is blocked (a dead sliding door, fire ahead), plan_route to "assembly" and move with the returned route_id.

TURN RULES
Think briefly — a few short sentences, this is an emergency — then make one tool call, for yourself only (actor_id "daniel"). While you are walking somewhere you keep going; you can still speak or look around. Read the result of your last action: never repeat a rejected call unchanged — follow its hint. Only cite evidence ids you know (they are listed under WHAT YOU KNOW). observe / plan_route / consult_plan move nobody; do not use them twice in a row without a reason.

TIME: 29.2 s
YOU: Daniel — in west exit (west_exit), standing still.
WHAT YOU KNOW:
- E1: fire — known burning in the cubicles, spreading; the nearest known flames are about 12 tiles from you.
ALARM: SOUNDING — the siren has alerted everyone in the building.
WITH YOU (can hear you): Maya (moving to the assembly point, 23 tiles left); Kenji (moving to the assembly point, 43 tiles left).
OTHERS: Alex — not in sight; Rosa — not in sight.
YOUR LATEST PLANNED ROUTE: R4 to assembly via west exit → outside → crosswalk → assembly point.
YOUR LAST ACTION: plan_route — Daniel's route to the assembly point: the west exit → outside → the crosswalk → the assembly point (47 tiles)

Decide your next action now — one tool call, for yourself.
